Calculate population-specific Fst (Weir & Goudet 2017)

Source: R/calculate_Fst.R
calculate_Fst.Rd

This function calculates population-specific Fst for each site using the allele-matching estimator of Weir & Goudet (2017). For each site, Fst compares the probability that two alleles drawn from different individuals within that site are identical (within-site matching) with the average probability that two alleles drawn from different sites are identical (between-site matching): \(F_{ST,i} = (M_i - M_B) / (1 - M_B)\).

Usage

calculate_Fst(gt, site_variable)

Arguments

gt

Genotype matrix where individuals are rows and loci are columns, coded as 0=aa, 1=aA, 2=AA.

site_variable

Vector of site IDs for each individual (same length as number of rows in gt). At least two sites are required.

Value

Named vector of Fst values, one per site.

Details

This is the population-specific counterpart of Weir & Cockerham's (1984) \(\theta\), and gives the same values as the Fs["Fst", ] row of hierfstat::fs.dosage(). Missing genotypes are handled as in hierfstat, by averaging matching over the loci genotyped in both individuals of a pair. Values are relative to the set of sites supplied, so they depend on which sites are included.

References

Weir, B. S., & Goudet, J. (2017). A unified characterization of population structure and relatedness. Genetics, 206(4), 2085–2103. https://doi.org/10.1534/genetics.116.198424

Weir, B. S., & Cockerham, C. C. (1984). Estimating F-statistics for the analysis of population structure. Evolution, 38(6), 1358–1370. https://doi.org/10.2307/2408641

Examples

data(example_data)
keep <- example_meta$population == 1
calculate_Fst(example_gt[keep, ], example_meta$site[keep])
